Name: Access Token
Description: A token used to access protected resources on behalf of an authenticated user. It is commonly used in OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect.

Name: Accessor
Description: An accessor is a method or property used to access or modify the internal state of an object. It provides controlled access to private or protected data.

Name: Aggregation
Description: Aggregation refers to the process of combining data from multiple sources or records into a single result. It is commonly used in databases, analytics, and reporting.

Name: Amazon Web Services
Description: AWS (Amazon Web Services) is Amazon’s cloud computing platform. It offers a wide range of services, including storage, compute, and databases.

Name: Amazon Web Services Software Development Kit
Description: A set of platform-specific building tools for developers to integrate and interact with AWS services in their applications. It provides APIs and libraries for AWS resources.

Name: Angular
Description: Angular is a popular open-source framework for building dynamic web applications. It uses TypeScript and provides features like data binding, routing, and dependency injection.

Name: Angular Web Mapping Framework
Description: is an extension of Angular for building interactive web maps and geospatial applications.

Name: API - Backend Implementation
Description: Software that implements a specification of requirements and its associated infrastructure. There are different implementation patterns depending on each use case.

Name: API - Consumer
Description: App that consumes an API.

Name: API - Consuming
Description: To consume an API means to use the API's endpoints to interact with it from another piece of software. This typically involves these steps: Understanding the API, sending requests, handling responses, handling errors. By consuming an API, a software application can leverage the functionality provided by the API, such as retrieving data, creating or modifying resources, or triggering actions.

Name: API - Consumption Plans
Description: Options that allow limiting the number of requests per second for each API / operation. They are defined closely linked to throttle policies (consumption per unit of time).

Name: API - Definition
Description: To define an API means to specify the methods and data formats that a program (typically a software library or service) will accept from other programs. This includes: Specifying the endpoints or URLs for the API (if it's a web-based API), defining the data types and structures that the API will accept as input or return as output, documenting the functionality of each method or endpoint, including what it does and any side effects it might have; setting up any necessary authentication or permission systems to control who can use the API and how; testing the API to ensure it works as expected and handles errors gracefully. This means: by defining an API, the contract created so other developers can rely on when integrating their software.

Name: API - Deployment
Description: To deploy an API  means to make it live and accessible on a server so that it can be used by other software applications. The process typically involves: Packaging choosing a deployment platform, configuring the server, uploading and starting the API and monitoring. By deploying an API with the Gluon pipelines, you make it available for other systems to interact with it, allowing data exchange and integration of services.

Name: API - Developer Portal
Description: Gives managed visibility to the produced APIs from the Producer Organization. Provides services as: APIs subscription, Socialization. Discovery. Feedback. Management of Consumer Organization.

Name: API - Entity
Description: Business object that has a sufficient relevance to identify itself as a product. A single entity is defined by an API.

Name: API - Implementation
Description: To implement an API  means to write the code that fulfills the contract defined by the API. It involves the following steps:  Understanding the API design, writing the code, testing, optimizing. Once an API is implemented, it means that the microservices which cover the business logic are ready to return the requested data.

Name: API - Portfolio
Description: Catalogue of APIs of an organization

Name: API - Producer
Description: An API producer builds and provides APIs for API consumers (app developers) to use.

Name: API - Resources
Description: A resource exposes a set of endpoints related to the same business entity.

Name: API - Publish
Description: To publish an API means to make it available for other developers to use. This process typically involves the following steps: Design; development; document creation; deploying, version set, monitoring and maintenance. By publishing an API, a service allows other software to interact with it programmatically, enabling integration and data exchange between different systems.

Name: API - Specification
Description: Document detailing the contract for an API and how to interact with it.

Name: API - Sub-entity
Description: Business object that have no business relevance by themselves. It is an object that is hierarchically related to an entity.

Name: API - Subscription
Description: To subscribe to an APItypically means to register or sign up to use that API. This process often involves: Signing up for an API key, accepting the terms of use, setting up a callback URL, handling API updates. Once you've subscribed to an API, your software application can begin consuming the API, meaning it can start making requests to the API's endpoints and using the data it receives in response.

Name: API - Terms
Description: Yaml parameters in URL, query, body or header in an API definition.

Name: API Connect (IBM)
Description: IBM API Connect is a full lifecycle API management solution that allows you to consistently create, manage, secure, socialize, and monetize APIs. It promotes digital transformation across clouds and on-premises environments.

Name: API Gateway
Description: Piece of software where APIs transactions are "physically" processed. It allows different consumption models related to the logical entities. It is unique by entity and consumer case. Included features: Authentication, Security policy enforcement, Load balancing, Cache management, Dependency resolution, Contract and service level agreement (SLA) management.

Name: API Gateway policy

Name: API Governance
Description: API governance is the practice of defining and applying standards, policies, and processes that ensure your APIs are standardized, reliable, and secure. It provides guardrails for creating, managing, and securing APIs.

Name: API Instance
Description: API deployed in a local gateway that implements exactly the same interface defined in the API published in Gluon catalog.

Name: API Management
Description: Process of creating and publishing APIs, enforcing their usage policies, controlling access, nurturing the subscriber community, collecting and analysing usage statistics, and reporting on performance. Implies the cataloguing of the API for its consumption (publishing), exposure (promoting), control, monitoring (overseeing) and execution in a safe, reliable and scalable environment.

Name: HTTP Response

Name: HTTP verb OPTIONS

Name: HTTP verb PATCH

Name: HTTP verb POST

Name: HTTP verb PUT

Name: HTTP Verbs

Description: TypeScript is a superset of JavaScript that adds static typing. It enhances code quality and provides better tooling for large-scale applications.

Name: Unary - (g)RPC
Description: Unary refers to a type of gRPC call where a client sends a single request to the server and receives a single response. It is a simple and common RPC pattern.

Name: UNICODE
Description: UNICODE is a character encoding standard that represents characters from various writing systems. It ensures consistent representation of text across different platforms.

Name: Unicode Transformation Format 8-bit
Description: UTF-8 (Unicode Transformation Format 8-bit) is a character encoding standard that represents characters using variable-length sequences of 8-bit bytes. It supports a wide range of characters and is commonly used for text files and web content.

Name: Uniform Resource Identifier
Description: Uniform Resource Identifier (URI) is a string that identifies a resource. URIs include URLs (web addresses) and URNs (names for resources).

Name: Uniform Resource Locator
Description: A Uniform Resource Locator (URL) is a web address that specifies the location of a resource on the internet. URLs are used to access websites, files, and other online content.

Name: Unit Tests
Description: Unit tests are small, automated tests that verify the correctness of individual components (units) of a software application. They focus on specific functions or methods.

Name: Universally Unique Identifier
Description: Universally Unique Identifier (UUID) is a 128-bit identifier that is unique across all devices and time. It is commonly used for generating unique keys.

Name: Unsafe Operation
Description: Unsafe operations imply a certain degree of criticality in their execution (generation of new resource, alteration of existing resource ...)

Name: User Agent
Description: A User Agent is a software application (usually a web browser) that acts on behalf of a user. It sends HTTP requests to web servers and renders web content.

Name: User Experience and User Interface
Description: User Experience (UX) and User Interface (UI) refer to the overall design and usability of a product. UX focuses on user satisfaction, while UI deals with visual elements and layout.

Name: User Interface
Description: User Interfaces (UIs) are the visual components of software applications that allow users to interact with the system. UIs can be graphical (GUI) or command-line (CLI).

Name: Validator
Description: Software component or tool that check the correctness, compliance, or integrity of data, configurations, or input.

Name: Vault
Description: A secure storage system for managing secrets, such as API keys, passwords, and encryption keys. It ensures sensitive data is stored securely and can be accessed by authorized applications.

Name: Version Type
Description: efers to the type or format of versioning used in software development. It could be semantic versioning (SemVer), incremental versioning, or custom versioning schemes.

Name: Virtualized
Description: Virtualized refers to running multiple instances of an OS or application on a single physical machine.

Name: Visual Studio Code
Description: A popular open-source code editor developed by Microsoft. It supports various programming languages and extensions.

Name: Web Application Firewall
Description: A Web Application Firewall (WAF) is a security solution that protects web applications from common attacks, such as SQL injection, cross-site scripting (XSS), and cross-site request forgery (CSRF). WAFs filter and monitor HTTP requests and responses.

Name: Web Client
Description: A Web Client is a user interface (such as a web browser) that interacts with web servers to request and display web content.

Name: Web Services Description Language
Description: Web Services Description Language (WSDL) is an XML-based language for describing web services. WSDL defines the operations, endpoints, and data types of a service.

Name: WebInspect - Microfocus
Description: WebInspect is a security testing tool by Micro Focus that scans web applications for vulnerabilities, including SQL injection, cross-site scripting (XSS), and more.

Name: World Wide Web Consortium
Description: The World Wide Web Consortium (W3C) is an international community that develops web standards and guidelines. W3C ensures interoperability and accessibility.

Name: X.509
Description: An ITU standard defining the format of public key certificates. X.509 certificates are used in many Internet protocols, including TLS/SSL (HTTPS).

Name: XML Localization Interchange File Format
Description: XLIFF (XML Localization Interchange File Format) is a standard for exchanging localization data. XLF files store translatable content and facilitate translation workflows.

Name: XRay - Jira
Description: XRay is a testing tool by JIRA that provides test management, execution, and reporting capabilities. It integrates with JIRA for tracking and managing test cases.

Name: Yaml
Description: YAML (YAML Yet Another Markup Language) is a human-readable data serialization format. It is commonly used for configuration files and data exchange.

Name: Yarn
Description: YARN (Yet Another Resource Negotiator) is a resource management layer in Hadoop clusters. It manages resources (CPU, memory) for running applications.
